Head and [muzzle](/wiki/Snout "Snout") appearance: field (left), and show (right), showing the shorter muzzle length, more solid appearance of the head, and "pronounced" stop of the latter

As a result of specialised breeding, there are significant differences between field and trial-bred and show-bred lines of Labradors. In the United States, the former are sometimes mistakenly referred to as "American" and the latter as "English". In fact, both field and show types are bred in both countries and all Labrador Retrievers are descended from British lines.[[18]](#cite_note-19)

In certain years, the Fields medalists have been officially cited for particular mathematical achievements, while in other years such specificities have not been given. However, in every year that the medal has been awarded, noted mathematicians have lectured at the [International Congress of Mathematicians](/wiki/International_Congress_of_Mathematicians "International Congress of Mathematicians") on each medalist's body of work. In the following table, official citations are quoted when possible (namely for the years 1958, 1998, and every year since 2006). For the other years through 1986, summaries of the ICM lectures, as written by Donald Albers, [Gerald L. Alexanderson](/wiki/Gerald_L._Alexanderson "Gerald L. Alexanderson"), and [Constance Reid](/wiki/Constance_Reid "Constance Reid"), are quoted.[[17]](#cite_note-17) In the remaining years (1990, 1994, and 2002), part of the text of the ICM lecture itself has been quoted. The upcoming awarding of the Fields Medal at the 2026 International Congress of the International Mathematical Union is planned to take place in [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia").[[18]](#cite_note-18)

fanoutqa_040102.x:
China National Petroleum Corporation :: Controversies :: Corruption allegations :: chunk_0012
In September 2013, [Jiang Jiemin](/wiki/Jiang_Jiemin "Jiang Jiemin"), a former chairman of PetroChina, a subsidiary of CNPC, was abruptly removed from his role as director of the [State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council](/wiki/State-owned_Assets_Supervision_and_Administration_Commission_of_the_State_Council "State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council") and investigated for corruption and abuse of power, along with four other senior oil executives.[[58]](#cite_note-59) [Jiang](/wiki/Jiang_Jiemin "Jiang Jiemin") was considered an ally of corrupt former security chief [Zhou Yongkang](/wiki/Zhou_Yongkang "Zhou Yongkang"), and part of a group of officials that had political ties with Zhou. On October 12, 2015, the court found [Jiang](/wiki/Jiang_Jiemin "Jiang Jiemin") guilty on all counts, including accepting bribes, possessing dark assets, and abusing his power. He was sentenced to 16 years in prison.[[59]](#cite_note-60)

In January 2017, former [PetroChina](/wiki/PetroChina "PetroChina") vice chairman [Liao Yongyuan](/wiki/Liao_Yongyuan "Liao Yongyuan") was sentenced to 15 years in prison for abuse of power and accepting nearly $2 million worth of bribes.[[60]](#cite_note-61)[[61]](#cite_note-62)

In October 2021, the [Central Commission for Discipline Inspection](/wiki/Central_Commission_for_Discipline_Inspection "Central Commission for Discipline Inspection") announced that it was investigating former [PetroChina](/wiki/PetroChina "PetroChina") vice president Ling Xiao, for "serious disciplinary violations."[[62]](#cite_note-63)

In 2014, Lanzhou Petrochemical, a subsidiary of CNPC, was responsible for ethylene and ammonia leaks, benzene contamination of water supplies, and air pollution in [Lanzhou](/wiki/Lanzhou "Lanzhou"). City officials criticized the company and demanded an apology.[[63]](

From 1980 to 2021 Microsoft released 9 [versions of MS-DOS](/wiki/Versions_of_MS-DOS "Versions of MS-DOS") and 13 [versions of Windows](/wiki/Versions_of_Windows "Versions of Windows"). The company's 1986 [initial public offering](/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") (IPO) and subsequent rise in its share price created three billionaires and an estimated 12,000 millionaires among Microsoft employees. Since the 1990s, it has increasingly diversified its business. [Steve Ballmer](/wiki/Steve_Ballmer "Steve Ballmer") replaced Gates as CEO in 2000. Poodle :: Health :: chunk_0009
The life expectancy of the Poodle varies based on size, as smaller dogs live longer than larger dogs.[[30]](#cite_note-30) A study in Japan found the Toy Poodle to have a life expectancy of 12.7 years.[[31]](#cite_note-31) A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14 years for the breed compared to an average of 12.7 for purebreeds and 12 for [crossbreeds](/wiki/Mongrel "Mongrel").[[32]](#cite_note-32) A 2005 Swedish study found 25% of miniature and toy Poodles died by the age of 10, less than the overall rate of 35% of dogs dying by the age of 10.[[33]](#cite_note-33)

Poodles suffer from a number of hereditary diseases. The Poodle Health Registry lists over 50 major health disorders of Standard Poodles.[[8]](#cite_note-:0-8) Some of the worst common hereditary poodle diseases are the skin disease [sebaceous adenitis](/wiki/Sebaceous_adenitis "Sebaceous adenitis") (estimated prevalence 2.7%) and [Addison's disease](/wiki/Addison%27s_disease_in_canines "Addison's disease in canines"), an endocrine system disorder. Both diseases became more prevalent in poodles after the 1960s burst in poodle popularity led to rapid breeding aimed at producing good show dogs. The breeding focused on a small number of popular bloodlines, creating a genetic bottleneck.[[34]](#cite_note-:3-34)[[8]](#cite_note-:0-8) One study estimated that two average Standard Poodles are about as closely related as the offspring of two full sibling [village dogs](/wiki/Village_dog "Village dog").[[34]](#cite_note-:3-34)

The Poodle is predisposed to the following dermatological conditions: [allergic skin disease](/w/index.php?title=Allergic_skin_disease&action=edit&redlink=1 "Allergic skin disease (page does not exist)"), [alopecia X](/wiki/Alopecia_X "Alopecia X") or follicular arrest, injection site alopecia, [otitis externa](/wiki/Otitis_externa "Otitis externa"), [melanoma](/wiki/Melanoma "Melanoma"), and [sebaceous adenitis](/wiki/Sebaceous_adenitis "Sebaceous adeni

Nanjing University's motto is "Sincerity with Aspiration, Perseverance with Integrity" (simplified Chinese: 诚朴雄伟 励学敦行; traditional Chinese: 誠樸雄偉 勵學敦行; pinyin: *chéng pǔ xióng wěi lì xué dūn xíng*).[[10]](#cite_note-nju_motto-10)[[11]](#cite_note-nju_motto_chinese-11) The first part of the motto, "Sincerity with Aspiration," originated during the university's period as the historical National Central University, while "Perseverance with Integrity" draws inspiration from classical Chinese aphorisms.[[12]](#cite_note-nju_motto_history_xiaobao-12)

Historically, [Li Ruiqing](/wiki/Li_Ruiqing "Li Ruiqing"), president of Liangjiang Higher Normal School, the precursor to Nanjing University, inscribed the motto "One who chews on the roots of vegetables can accomplish great things" (Chinese: 嚼得菜根 做得大事; pinyin: *jiáo dé cài gēn zuò dé dà shì*).[[12]](#cite_note-nju_motto_history_xiaobao-12) Later, during the National Central University era, President [Luo Jialun](/wiki/Luo_Jialun "Luo Jialun") formally adopted "Sincerity with Aspiration" as the university's motto. Following the establishment of the People's Republic of China in 1949, Nanjing University underwent a series of reorganizations and consolidations, and a formal motto was not established for an extended period.[[12]](#cite_note-nju_motto_history_xiaobao-12) The current motto, "Sincerity with Aspiration, Perseverance with Integrity", was adopted during the university's centennial celebration in 2002 under the leadership of then-President [Jiang Shusheng](/wiki/Jiang_Shusheng "Jiang Shusheng"), following extensive consultation with faculty and students.[[13]](#cite_note-nju_motto_jiangshusheng-13)

Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Justin Bieber](/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Justin_Bieber "List of awards and nominations received by Justin Bieber")

Throughout his career, Bieber has sold an estimated 150 million records worldwide, making him one of the [best-selling music artists of all time](/wiki/List_of_best-selling_music_artists "List of best-selling music artists").[[254]](#cite_note-254)[[255]](#cite_note-Kilkenny-255)

In 2011, Bieber was honoured with a star in front of Avon Theater in [Stratford, Ontario](/wiki/Stratford,_Ontario "Stratford, Ontario"), Canada, where he used to busk when he was younger. On November 23, 2012, Bieber was presented with the [Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal](/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II_Diamond_Jubilee_Medal "Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal") by the former Prime Minister of Canada, [Stephen Harper](/wiki/Stephen_Harper "Stephen Harper"). He was one of 60,000 Canadians to receive the Diamond Jubilee medal that year.[[256]](#cite_note-256) In 2013, Bieber received a [Diamond award](/wiki/Diamond_award "Diamond award") from the [Recording Industry Association of America](/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for his single "[Baby](/wiki/Baby_(Justin_Bieber_song) "Baby (Justin Bieber song)")", which at the time became the [highest-certified digital single of all time](/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles_in_the_United_States "List of best-selling singles in the United States").[[257]](#cite_note-257)[[258]](#cite_note-258) Bieber is credited with five [Diamond](/wiki/Diamond_Certified "Diamond Certified") certifications from the RIAA.[[9]](#cite_note-ReferenceA-9) Bieber has won two [Grammy Awards](/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") out of 23 nominations,[[259]](#cite_note-GRAMMY_Awards-259) one [Latin Grammy Award](/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award "Latin Grammy Awa

The **deputy prime minister of Singapore**[[a]](#cite_note-1) is the deputy [head of government](/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of the [Republic of Singapore](/wiki/Republic_of_Singapore "Republic of Singapore"), and a key political ally of the [prime minister](/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Singapore "Prime Minister of Singapore"). The incumbent deputy prime minister is [Gan Kim Yong](/wiki/Gan_Kim_Yong "Gan Kim Yong"), an MP for [Punggol Group Representation Constituency](/wiki/Punggol_Group_Representation_Constituency "Punggol Group Representation Constituency") from the governing [People's Action Party](/wiki/People%27s_Action_Party "People's Action Party"), who took office on 15 May 2024.
